quick: 50-100 mg PO TID; titrate to max 800 mg/day
Use only if clearly needed; neonatal effects in 3rd trimester
Use with caution; no specific adjustment defined
summary: Thioridazine is a piperidine phenothiazine antipsychotic reserved for schizophrenia refractory to other antipsychotics because of dose-related QTc prolongation, torsades de pointes and sudden death. It also carries the class warning of increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Baseline and follow-up ECG and electrolytes are essential.
indications: Management of schizophrenia in patients who fail to respond adequately to other antipsychotic drugs (after at least two adequate trials of different agents)

dosage.n: Reserve for failure of other antipsychotics
Max 800 mg/day; use lowest effective dose
For severe disturbance unresponsive to other therapy

admin: Obtain baseline ECG and serum potassium before starting
Individualize dose; use the smallest effective dose
Correct hypokalemia before and during therapy
Avoid other QT-prolonging drugs and CYP2D6 inhibitors
Reduce dose gradually when discontinuing to avoid withdrawal
moa: Thioridazine blocks postsynaptic dopamine D2 receptors in mesolimbic pathways, producing antipsychotic effect. It also has substantial anticholinergic, antihistaminic and alpha-adrenergic blocking activity. Blockade of cardiac potassium (IKr) channels underlies its dose-dependent QTc prolongation.

absolute: Severe CNS depression or comatose states
Congenital long QT syndrome or history of cardiac arrhythmias
Concomitant drugs that prolong QTc or are potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., fluvoxamine, propranolol, pindolol, fluoxetine)
relative: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality)
monitor: Signs of tardive dyskinesia or neuroleptic malignant syndrome

preg: Use only if clearly needed. Neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms after delivery; monitor the newborn.
lact: Avoid. Phenothiazines are excreted in breast milk and may cause sedation in the infant.
renal: Use with caution; no specific dose adjustment is defined in the label. Monitor clinically.
hepatic: Use with caution and avoid in significant hepatic impairment; phenothiazines can cause cholestatic jaundice and are hepatically metabolized.

major: Potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine) - contraindicated; raise thioridazine and QT risk
Propranolol, pindolol - contraindicated; increase thioridazine levels
Other QT-prolonging drugs (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, methadone, macrolides, some antibiotics) - additive torsades risk
moderate: CNS depressants, alcohol, opioids - additive sedation/respiratory depression
minor: Antacids - reduced absorption if taken together
interactions.food: No specific food interaction; may be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive CNS depression and hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive pregnancy/phenylketonuria urine tests; prolongs QTc on ECG; may alter thyroid uptake tests.

emergency: Torsades de pointes / ventricular arrhythmia / sudden cardiac death
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Serum potassium and magnesium (correct before/during therapy)
Ophthalmologic exam with prolonged high-dose use (retinopathy)
Assess for extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia
counsel: This medicine is reserved for when other antipsychotics have not worked
Report fainting, palpitations or irregular heartbeat immediately
Avoid alcohol and other sedating drugs
Report uncontrolled movements, fever with muscle stiffness, or vision changes
pk: Antipsychotic effect over days to weeks
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), protect from light
pearls: Reserved second/third-line because of dose-related QT prolongation and sudden death
Contraindicated with CYP2D6 inhibitors and other QT-prolonging drugs
Check ECG and potassium before and during therapy
Highest retinotoxic potential among phenothiazines - avoid >800 mg/day
Class warning: increased mortality in elderly dementia patients
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose can cause severe cardiac arrhythmias (torsades), QT prolongation, hypotension, CNS depression and seizures. Provide cardiac monitoring and supportive care; treat arrhythmias avoiding agents that further prolong QT (avoid quinidine/disopyramide/procainamide). Manage hypotension without epinephrine (paradoxical hypotension). Dialysis is not effective.
